biggest_catch: This only pays off if you actually paid an early-termination fee to your old provider - it is reimbursement of a cost you already incurred, not free money - and you must repay Amigo if you leave them within 12 months.
catches: Only available on Amigo Energy Texas term agreements of 12 months or more.
You must submit your old provider's final bill showing the cancellation fee within 90 days of enrollment.
The credit is applied only after your first full-service period bill with Amigo is paid in full.
You must repay the reimbursement to Amigo Energy if you switch away within 12 months of starting your Agreement.

c3.evidence: Incentive framed as savings on planned energy spending (bill credit), not income.

c4.evidence: Mechanism is distinct from R1880 (Amigo referral) and R1881 (Amigo demand-response); cancellation-fee reimbursement verified on same official domain.

eligibility: New Amigo Energy Texas customers on term agreements of 12+ months who paid an early-termination/cancellation fee to their previous electric provider.
notes: Cancellation-fee reimbursement framed as savings on planned energy spending, never income. Repayment clause if customer switches away within 12 months. Distinct from R1880 (Amigo refer-a-friend) and R1881 (Amigo demand-response rewards).
numeric_basis: payout up to $150 from official page text ('reimburse up to $150', applied as a bill credit); time: 15-30 minutes for switching/signup per user constraint
payout_quote: We're always looking to make electricity transfer easier, which is why we're ready to reimburse up to $150 of the cancellation fee your old provider charges. Specifically, this applies for Texas electricity plans with term agreements of 12 months or more.
payout_value_note: Up to $150 as a bill credit reimbursing the cancellation fee charged by the previous provider; actual amount depends on the fee the customer paid (up to $150).

s1.note: New Amigo Energy Texas customer on a term agreement of 12 months or greater.

s2.note: Paid a cancellation/early-termination fee to the previous electric provider.

s3.note: Submit the old provider's final bill showing the cancellation fee within 90 days of enrollment.

s4.note: Credit posts as a bill credit after the first full-service-period bill with Amigo is paid in full.

s5.note: Retention risk: reimbursement must be repaid to Amigo Energy if the customer switches away within 12 months of starting the Agreement.

s6.note: No direct cash payout; credit applies to the Amigo Energy bill only.

s7.note: Texas deregulated areas only, per page FAQ.

steps: Compare and enroll in an Amigo Energy Texas plan with a term of 12 months or more.
Keep the final bill from your previous provider that shows the cancellation fee.
Submit that bill within 90 days of enrollment via email to customersupport@amigoenergy.com, mail, or fax.
Pay your first full-service-period Amigo Energy bill in full; the reimbursement credit is applied to your account.
timing: Switching/signup is 15-30 minutes of active effort; the credit appears after the first full-service-period bill is paid in full.
